description:
I'm an ICT Application Development developer from South Africa with a strong interest in AI, space technology, Earth observation, environmental intelligence and building practical systems around complex problems.

I'm developing Eyes on Fires - FIRMS Constellation & Earth Intelligence Explorer, an interactive wildfire intelligence platform that combines a 3D Earth interface with NASA satellite observations, environmental data and scientific research tools.
summary:
Eyes on Fires is an interactive Earth-observation platform that brings NASA FIRMS active-fire and thermal-anomaly detections into a custom 3D WebGL globe. Users can explore satellite observations, inspect detection locations, follow satellite orbital paths, replay historical observation windows and investigate documented wildfire events.

Its Earth Intelligence system combines atmospheric and land-condition layers, including temperature, humidity, vapor pressure deficit, wind, precipitation, soil moisture, vegetation stress and lightning-related atmospheric context. Historical reanalysis, live conditions and numerical weather forecasts are distinguished to preserve data provenance.

The platform also incorporates the Canadian Fire Weather Index to visualize weather-based fire danger, alongside a scientific research environment for analyzing observations and investigating wildfire prediction methodologies.

Powered by AMFI and CouncilRise, the project aims to move beyond simply visualizing detected fires towards understanding environmental conditions and developing scientifically defensible approaches to anticipating future wildfire occurrences.
details:
Eyes on Fires is a browser-based Earth-observation and wildfire intelligence platform designed to bring satellite observations, environmental conditions and historical wildfire information together in one interactive geographical environment.

What it does

The platform uses a custom GPU-accelerated WebGL 3D Earth globe to visualize NASA FIRMS active-fire and thermal-anomaly observations from MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments. Users can rotate and explore the Earth, switch between visible Earth and nighttime views, inspect individual detection locations, view satellite orbital paths and navigate historical observation windows.

Its Earth Intelligence interface provides selectable geographical layers for:

  • Temperature and atmospheric humidity.
  • Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD).
  • Wind speed, direction and animated wind vectors.
  • Precipitation and accumulated rainfall.
  • Soil moisture and vegetation stress.
  • Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) and lightning-related atmospheric context.
  • Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index (FWI).

Historical ERA5-Land reanalysis, live meteorological conditions and numerical weather forecasts are maintained as distinct temporal modes. The FWI implementation provides a weather-based fire-danger indicator, not a direct probability of ignition.

Scientific research and innovation

The platform includes a Science Lab for satellite constellation analysis, detection metrics, geospatial clustering, source-quality checks, historical fire stories and research evidence.

Its underlying research programme, AMFI (Adaptive Multi-System Fire Intelligence), investigates how wildfire occurrence, satellite detection and environmental conditions can be understood more reliably.

Supported by CouncilRise, a personal made AI-assisted scientific research system, AMFI has conducted experiments into recurrence versus new documented fire events, satellite observation coverage, event timelines, cloud-mask interpretation, detection uncertainty and prediction methodology.

A significant research finding was that repeated fire activity and new documented fire events should be treated as distinct prediction targets. Further experiments also identified important limitations in satellite observability and historical event documentation.

Benefits and intended impact

Eyes on Fires makes complex Earth-observation information easier to explore, understand and investigate. It encourages more responsible interpretation of satellite detections by distinguishing observed thermal anomalies from independently confirmed wildfire events.

Its longer-term ambition is to investigate whether combining satellite observations, weather forecasts, vegetation conditions, soil moisture, lightning, terrain and human-related ignition factors can support more reliable early wildfire warnings.

Technology

The platform was developed using Python 3.12, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, custom WebGL rendering, NumPy and SciPy. It uses a Python REST API and is deployed as a web application through Render.

Its research and data pipeline works with NASA FIRMS, NASA LAADS DAAC, MODIS, VIIRS and GOES satellite products, Copernicus ERA5-Land, Open-Meteo meteorological services and historical wildfire records.

Creative approach and scientific considerations

The project combines a 3D satellite exploration interface with environmental intelligence and an AI-assisted research methodology. Rather than presenting every satellite hotspot as a confirmed fire, the system considers geographic coverage, pixel footprints, sensor viewing geometry, cloud conditions, event timing, data completeness and observation uncertainty.

The system deliberately distinguishes fire detection, fire danger and prospective ignition prediction. Validated operational wildfire ignition predictions have not yet been established.

Long-term vision

The ambition is to evolve Eyes on Fires into an adaptive wildfire intelligence platform that connects global Earth observations with environmental science and experimentally validated predictive methodologies, helping researchers and communities better understand wildfire threats.
